blocks.h2: Why a Sewer Scope Matters When Buying in Evanston
blocks.body: In Evanston, the lateral belongs to the property owner, and on an older house it may be close to 100 years old. A sewer scope during your inspection period shows whether the line is clean, needs a cleaning or needs a repair. That footage gives you facts to negotiate with, before closing. It's a small cost compared to finding out after you move in, when the repair is fully yours.

blocks.h2: Sewer Camera Questions From Evanston Homeowners

items.q: Should I scope the sewer before buying in Evanston?
items.answer: Yes. The lateral is the owner's responsibility here, and a home inspection doesn't usually cover it.

items.q: Can you tell where the break is?
items.answer: Yes. We mark the spot on the surface and note the depth, so any repair is targeted.

items.q: Can you see where my line meets the city sewer?
items.answer: Usually, yes. That shows whether a problem is in your lateral or at the connection.
Yes. Share it with a seller, your agent or another contractor.

items.q: How soon can you inspect during a home sale?
items.answer: Usually within a few days, so it fits your inspection window.

items.q: Can a camera tell me how old my sewer line is?
items.preview: It shows the material, which hints at age.
items.answer: It shows the pipe material and condition, which usually tells us roughly when it was installed.

items.q: How much does a sewer camera inspection cost in Evanston?
items.preview: It depends on access and length. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on access and the length of the line. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
